topics.label: Introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the session by connecting histopathology practicals to molecular mechanisms and outlining the key learning objectives.

topics.label: Tumor viruses, proto-oncogene discovery, and transformation assays
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how the historical study of transforming viruses led to the discovery of cellular proto-oncogenes and the experimental assays used to test cellular transformation.

topics.label: Functional classification and genetics of oncogenes and tumor suppressors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the functional definitions of cancer mutations and illustrate the genetics of oncogenes and tumor suppressors through the Rb and p53 pathways.

topics.label: Mechanisms and consequences of genomic instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the distinct origins, repair pathways, and cellular stress consequences of sequence instability and chromosomal instability in cancer.

topics.label: Multi-step progression, hereditary predisposition, and tumor dynamics
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how stepwise mutation accumulation drives tumor progression and how inherited cancer predispositions and ongoing genetic instability shape tumor development.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and reading recommendations
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the lecture with closing remarks, recommended reading, and a preview of the next session.
